interpretation: A contraction is a controlled change of tropical presentation: adjoining a coordinate turns a regular function into a geometric full graph whose exceptional vertical fibers make its zero behavior visible, while projection forgets that auxiliary coordinate and collapses precisely those fibers. Weighting the new facets retains the zero multiplicity of g through the pole order of its reciprocal; restricting the auxiliary coordinate to finite values produces a principal open model. The gain is an explicit weighted space on which balancing is stated to hold, while the loss under projection is the auxiliary-coordinate and vertical-fiber structure; the span states, but does not prove, the balancing proposition.

Project back to V to contract the added structure, iterate principal contractions for more coordinates, or retain only the finite auxiliary-coordinate part to form the associated principal open set.
